projects.title: Outrider RC Car
projects.summary: My biggest build yet: a full RC vehicle designed end to end, from ESP32 firmware and a custom controller PCB to the chassis and its own branding. Driving, steering and lights already work. It isn't finished yet, but it will be soon.
projects.about:
Outrider is a complete RC vehicle system that I'm building from the ground up, covering the firmware, the electronics, the physical design and the branding.

An ESP32 connects to an Xbox Series X controller over Bluetooth, drives the motor through a BTS7960 motor driver and steers with a servo. Motor control, steering and the lighting system are all working.

The project isn't complete yet, but it will be soon. This page will be updated as the final build comes together.
features: ESP32 firmware that pairs with an Xbox Series X controller over Bluetooth
Motor control through a BTS7960 driver using ESP32-native LEDC PWM
Servo steering with a tuned joystick deadzone
Lighting system with headlights, hazards and turn indicators on the controller bumpers
Custom 190 × 140 mm controller PCB, fabricated by PCBWay
High-current external power switch: through-hole pads wired to a panel-mount slide switch on the +12 V rail
Overlander-style body concept and "Outrider" stickers for the PCB panels
projects.challenges:
The BTS7960 library I started with only supported AVR boards, so I replaced it with ESP32-native LEDC PWM functions.

The steering initially went the wrong way. The Xbox controller library was returning joystick values as unsigned numbers instead of signed ones, so I fixed the conversion and corrected the steering direction. I also had to resolve GPIO pin conflicts on the ESP32.

Before ordering the PCB I reviewed the Gerber files and found an empty Edge_Cuts layer, which I fixed before submitting the order to PCBWay.

sections.heading: Chassis and body
sections.body: I analysed an existing 1/10 scale RC truck chassis (about 294 mm wheelbase) from its STL file, then generated a parametric tube-frame buggy chassis in OpenSCAD with rendered previews. The body is an overlander-style concept, drawn in SVG.

sections.heading: Tuning notes
sections.body: Confirmed working values in the firmware: joyDeadzone = 200, centerPulse = 1200, maxOffset = 650, with the steering servo on GPIO 19.

projects.title: Filing Cabinet
projects.summary: A filing cabinet built from 3/4" birch plywood, with soft-close runners, a black stain and a chrome handle.
projects.about: Built from 3/4" Birch Plywood to store all of my important documents. With a soft close drawer runner ensuring a premium feel. Couple that with a black stain and a chrome handle to match the rest of the furniture, suddenly a premium looking piece of furniture has been built.
projects.challenges: Ensuring a perfect 90 degree join for all of the corners, especially with basic equipment. Along with this, to keep the premium feel of the cabinet I needed to make sure there was an equal surround around all 4 sides of the drawer front. I used playing cards to achieve this.
projects.learned: An understanding of how to achieve a high-end finish on something that does not have to cost the earth. Sometimes a simpler solution can work just as well as a manufactured jig (playing cards).

projects.title: GCSE Technology and Design Coursework Project
projects.summary: A year-long GCSE Technology and Design project: a handheld reaction timer for motorsport drivers and athletes, taken from concept through to a working prototype.
projects.about:
A full year GCSE Technology and Design coursework project demonstrating comprehensive design and manufacturing skills. This project shows the entire design process from concept through testing.

The product is a handheld reaction timer shaped like a gaming controller, designed for motorsport drivers, athletes and gym users. Five LEDs light up and go out at a random time; the user presses a button as fast as they can and their reaction time is shown on an LCD screen to three decimal places. It runs on a 9 V battery inside a 3D-printed PLA case.
projects.challenges: Managing a year-long project required planning, time management, and the ability to adapt designs based on practical constraints. Balancing aesthetic design with functional engineering was challenging.
projects.learned: This extensive project taught me about the complete design-to-manufacturing pipeline, problem-solving under constraints, resource management, and iterative improvement through testing and feedback.

projects.title: Ski Trip Organiser – GCSE Digital Technology
projects.summary: GCSE Digital Technology coursework: a C# program that helps a teacher assign pupils on a school ski trip to the right ski group.
projects.about:
A coursework project for GCSE Digital Technology that demonstrates the ability to create a functional application addressing a real-world problem.

The brief was a school ski trip: the organiser needed a way to assign each pupil to a beginner, intermediate or advanced group, based on their dry ski slope times and a quiz on ski safety.

projects.learned: This GCSE coursework project taught me how to approach a problem systematically, design solutions, implement them in code, and test thoroughly. I learned about user requirements and designing software to meet specific needs.
